debugging: Diagnose or repair existing behavior that is failing, incorrect, or inconsistent with its stated contract. Includes exceptions, wrong results, regressions, and explaining why a concrete failure happens. Own the diagnosis, fix, and associated regression tests together. Adding tests to verify a repair does not make this test generation; changing code to restore intended behavior is not new feature generation.
code_generation: Implement a new capability or intentionally change the design of working code. Includes adding an API, extending functionality, or refactoring without a concrete failure driving the request. Supporting tests belong with this implementation. Do not select this merely because code must change: restoring broken existing behavior belongs to debugging, and a tests-only request belongs to test generation.
test_generation: Create or extend automated tests for supplied existing behavior. Includes unit tests, edge-case coverage, fixtures, mocks, and parameterized cases when the requested deliverable is tests rather than production-code changes. Do not select this for a concrete failure that must be diagnosed or fixed, even if regression tests are also requested. Tests accompanying a new feature stay with code generation.
code_review: Inspect supplied code or changes and report actionable defects, risks, or quality problems without implementing repairs. The requested deliverable is findings and recommendations about whether the code is sound. Distinguish evaluation from neutral explanation of how code works. Diagnosing a specified observed failure belongs to debugging; implementing requested changes belongs to the appropriate writing agent.
repository_qa: Explain or locate existing repository code using available context. Includes describing control flow, dependencies, ownership, function behavior, and where functionality is implemented. The user wants understanding or navigation, not code edits, defect findings, or tests. Explaining why a concrete observed failure happens is debugging, while evaluating code for potential defects is code review.
fallback: The request is outside these coding-agent scopes, or essential information needed to select and perform the requested task is missing. Ask for the missing code, behavior, or context instead of inventing it. Includes unrelated non-coding requests and tasks requiring unavailable repository details. A supported coding request with enough supplied context should go to its specific owning agent.
